claim: There exists one compactly supported absolutely continuous probability measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R\) such that, for every \(0<\beta<1/3\), \[|\widehat{\mu}(\xi)|\le C_\beta(1+|\xi|)^{-\beta}\quad(\xi\in\mathbb R),\] while the dyadic lacunary maximal operator \(M_\mu f(x)=\sup_{k\in\mathbb Z}|f*\mu_k(x)|\) is unbounded from \(H^1(\mathbb R)\) to \(L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R)\).

integrity.proof_type: analytic proof with probabilistic existence lemma and explicit scale estimates

scientific_limitations: The decay bound is proved for every exponent strictly below 1/3, not at 1/3.
The optimal Fourier-decay threshold is not determined.
The construction is one-dimensional, absolutely continuous, and not asserted to have a smooth or bounded density.
title: A near-third Fourier-decay exponent for endpoint-failing lacunary maximal measures
